conclusions: Full nesting breaks under reset updates in all controls; it is distinct from the center-directed partial relation.
Both active pc and pp hold in every recorded chain snapshot. All seven cases pass active pc and newly committed edge pc.

Main relative fix: Guard creates one center-directed candidate-child membership gap after pass3; updating cut45 in pass4 repairs it. A child candidate list at raw algebraic capacity16 has only15 unique samples and misses child9, while sample11 is duplicated.

The paired Guard append and raw-dimension capacity path permits candidate closure gaps through inactive child cuts. Duplicates alone are allowed by CandidateSets. Inspect this path alongside mixed-capacity work in854/794; no production change is made here.
Candidate closure gaps also occur in baseline and convergent controls; a cause of late rank cycling is not established.
Main relative fix passes39-50 have no new Guard pivots, unchanged maximum rank372, and stability_counter1 because smaller cuts still regrow.
The R4 CTTN control has ten active pp failure snapshots but no active pc failures and converges in4. Chain pp results do not establish a universal tree invariant.

Absolute control differs from original M6a ranks starting pass27 and errors starting pass28, although both converge46. Clean and instrumented versions agree; cross-harness divergence remains unresolved.
No numerical tolerance, stopping condition, pass limit, Guard rule or selection policy was changed. Numerical interpolation and conditioning remain untested by this structural audit.

paper.scope: Reset two-site chain TCI distinguishes full and partial nesting. The diagnostic center-directed tree interpretation is not a general numerical proof.
